mentions.name: Uruky
mentions.description: A private, paid, ad-free, personally customizable search engine. Signup requires no personal information (a randomly-generated account number is assigned), and a proof-of-work captcha grants 2 hours of free use. Users can pick among many search providers for defaults and per query, including Uruky Site Search, which is powered by the project's own index that is growing slowly with a focus on the indie/small web. Recently shipped features include an image search gallery mode, a calculator and conversion widget, and Tags and Scopes. After 12 months as a paying customer, users receive a copy of the source code (licensed BUSL, converting to AGPLv3 in 2 years).
mentions.problem: Offers a private, ad-free alternative to ad-driven search engines; the main ongoing challenge is discoverability and outreach, which is handled ethically without Big Tech or generative AI/LLMs.

mentions.name: Uruky
mentions.description: A private, paid, ad-free, and personally customizable search engine. Signup requires no personal information — a randomly generated account number is assigned — and a proof-of-work captcha grants 2 hours of free use. Users can choose among many search providers for defaults and per query, including Uruky Site Search, which powers its own index (being slowly increased with a focus on the indie/small web). Recent features include an image search gallery mode and a new sponsorships page, and payments are supported in Monero and Bitcoin via ProxyStore. After 12 months as a paying customer, users receive a copy of the source code (BUSL, converting to AGPLv3 in 2 years). The project also sponsors open source projects and maintainers, plus indie, small-web, and privacy-related sites and groups.

mentions.name: Uruky
mentions.description: A paid, privacy-focused web search engine based in the EU, positioned as a simpler Kagi alternative. It supports Monero payments via ProxyStore, offers a free 2-hour trial gated by a local proof-of-work captcha (Altcha), is growing its own search index focused on the indie/small web with more search providers planned, and gives customers a copy of the source code after 12 months of paying (licensed BUSL, converting to AGPLv3 in 2 years).
